## Description
Fixed the bug [#3327](https://github.com/Textualize/rich/issues/3327).

Changes -
1. Added '@' in rich.highlighter:ReprHighlighter url regex pattern.
2. Added a test case in test_highlighter for the url with '@'.

FILES: rich/highlighter.py:102
ROOT CAUSE: The URL regex pattern in `ReprHighlighter` does not include the '@' character, which causes hyperlinks containing credentials (e.g., `https://user:pass@host.com`) to be highlighted incorrectly.
CHANGE: Add `@` to the character class in the `url` regex pattern: `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"` becomes `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~@]*)"`.
TEST: tests/test_highlighter.py

I have fixed the bug where the `@` character broke highlighting in hyperlinks by updating the `url` regex pattern in `rich/highlighter.py` to include the `@` character.

Changed `rich/highlighter.py`:
- Updated the `url` regex in `ReprHighlighter` from `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"` to `r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~@]*)".`

To verify the fix, you can run the tests in `tests/test_highlighter.py`.
